Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
311 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 311 AM EDT Friday...

No changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 311 AM EDT Friday...

1. Dry, clear, and seasonably cool weather will lead to 
pleasant, fall-like, conditions today and most of tomorrow. Light 
shower chances will approach southern Vermont late Saturday, with a 
weak frontal passage across the north and central portions of the 
area Sunday.

2. Patchy frost possible on Tuesday morning, followed by warmer 
and unsettled weather for mid to late next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 311 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A picture perfect start the weekend looks to be in store 
beginning today through Saturday. Temperatures will trend slightly 
below seasonable levels today as northwest flow advects cooler air 
from Canada. Highs will be in the mid 60s to near 70 with clear 
skies. A few light breezes near the International Border, and 
Champlain Valley, to 10-15 MPH could bring a slight bite to the air 
Friday afternoon. Clear skies will persist through tonight with 
areawide strong radiational cooling. Temperatures will cool into the 
low to mid 40s for most locations, and near 50 for areas around Lake 
Champlain. Raw guidance denotes low to mid 30s for areas in the 
heart of the Adirondacks. Tonight looks like the better night for 
patchy valley fog in the favored river valleys of Vermont and 
northern New York. Though it will not be widespread fog with it 
being 2 days detached from rain. Nonetheless, areas near Montpelier, 
the lamoille Valley, CT river, and sheltered areas of the 
Adirondacks have a good chance for patchy fog. Saturday looks to be 
a repeat of Friday with slightly warmer highs into the mid to upper 
40s with mostly clear skies. Gusty channeled winds in the Champlain 
Valley, and mountain summit winds, will be possible by Saturday 
afternoon with winds turning more southerly, hence our warmer 
temperature advection. Winds could gusts up to 25 MPH will be 
possible, with locally higher on Lake Champlain itself. A Lake Wind 
Advisory may be needed during the day Saturday through Saturday 
evening. 

Saturday looks to remain dry up until the late evening. A weak 
shortwave looks to pass just to our south, brining some light shower 
chances to southern Vermont, mainly along or south of US-4. Showers 
will be confined to the overnight hours, shifting east by sunrise. 
Overnight lows Saturday will be mild as a result into the upper 50s 
to low 60s. Clouds associated with the showers will build across the 
region keeping the area socked in with cloud cover on Sunday. A 
frontal passage will bring additional shower chances to the central 
and northern portions of the areas. Showers will be scattery and 
broken in nature. Model soundings do show the potential for some 
isolated rumbles of thunder, mainly across northern New York, but 
any storms will be weak with limited instability, and lagging 
dynamics. Temperatures will return to seasonably cool level in the 
60s by Monday, with drying conditions.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A fast/progressive flow aloft prevails acrs the northern 
CONUS for next week as our cwa remains in the battle ground btwn 
very warm/moist airmass over the Ohio/Mississippi Valleys and much 
cooler/drier air to the north over central Canada. As boundary 
sharpens acrs the Mid Atlantic/NE CONUS for mid to late next week, 
potential for widespread precipitation increases for our region. 
Still a large spread in potential solutions from the globe guidance 
and associated ensemble members on placement and timing of heaviest 
precip, given fast flow aloft and some agreement of boundary 
paralleling the mid/upper lvl winds. 

Progged 1025mb high pres directly overhead on Tues morning wl 
produce light winds and clear skies with valley fog and pockets of 
patchy frost possible. Lows range from near freezing SLK/NEK to 
upper 40s near Lake Champlain. First weak boundary and associated 
s/w energy drops acrs our cwa late Tues into Weds with ribbon of 
enhanced mid lvl moisture, but limited instability. Expect a brief 
period of rain showers with latest WPC still indicating chc-likely 
(40 to 70%) pops. Also, progged 850mb winds of 30 to 40 knots are 
expected acrs our cwa ahead of approaching boundary on Tues, so 
anticipated breezy south to southwest winds, especially 
central/northern CPV and higher trrn of dacks/northern Greens. Temps 
wl warm into the mid 70s to lower 80s per latest WPC fcst. Temps wl 
be highly depend upon what side of the boundary our cwa wl be on for 
mid to late week, along with areas of clouds/precip. WPC has highs 
in the upper 60s to mid 70s with lows mid 40s to mid 50s for Weds 
thru Friday, which looks reasonable attm.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...VFR conditions will prevail at our taf
sites for the next 12 to 18 hours, with a low probability (<10%)
of localized fog/br at MPV/SLK toward sunrise this morning.
Current analysis places 1018mb low pres near Flint MI with 
cyclonic northwest flow and mid level clouds across our taf 
sites. Clearing is approaching the International Border and 
should be across our region by sunrise, which could result in 
some very localized patchy fog/br near SLK/MPV. Otherwise, VFR 
with mostly clear skies prevails today with northwest winds 4 to
8 knots, except a few gusts 12 to 18 knots near MPV. 

Outlook...

Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Sunday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA, Slight chance
TSRA.
Sunday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. Chance SHRA.

&&
